stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model near Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol at $1.50/$7.50

key_facts.fact: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov. 12, 2026, built for speed and efficiency in everyday coding and agentic workflows, complementing frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

key_facts.fact: Hydrogen is priced flat across its 1M-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Google says Hydrogen beats Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at default high thinking (51 vs 50), reaching 54 at its new xhigh setting.
key_facts.excerpt: Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting)

key_facts.fact: Versus Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5x faster, more than triples Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs 18.2%) and cuts fabricated claims by more than 5x.
key_facts.excerpt: Hydrogen finishes "tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting" ... "more than [triples] Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%)" ... Cuts "fabricated claims by more than 5x"

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis puts Hydrogen (xhigh) 1 point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, at ~32% of Sonnet's cost per task but ~2.5x that of GPT-6.1 Sol.
key_facts.excerpt: places it 1 point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max), at ~32% of Sonnet's cost but ~2.5x that of GPT-6.1 Sol

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis measured an 8% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience, versus 43% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and 52% for GPT-6.1 Sol, but weaker agentic terminal work (54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 vs 64% for Sonnet 5.5).
key_facts.excerpt: Hydrogen has one of the lowest hallucination rates recorded at 8%, compared with 43% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and 52% for GPT-6.1 Sol (max) ... Hydrogen scores 54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 ... Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) scores 64%

key_facts.fact: Hydrogen is rolling out globally across the Gemini API, AI Studio, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search (all users) and Antigravity for paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
key_facts.excerpt: for all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory, AI agents that pentest and patch code

key_facts.fact: At its Cyber at the Frontier event on Nov. 12, OpenAI announced two Daybreak security products: Red Team for penetration testing and Defense Factory for finding and fixing vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: The products, Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, were announced at the company's Cyber at the Frontier event on November 12.

key_facts.fact: Daybreak Red Team, in early access, uses fleets of agents with source code and app context to test web applications and validate findings from scanners, bug bounties and disclosure reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Red Team, which is available in early access, uses OpenAI models to test companies' web applications for vulnerabilities... with a fleet of agents using source code and app context to investigate and test attack paths.

key_facts.fact: Defense Factory agents, built on GPT-6 Cyber, scan codebases and prepare patches; engineers review fixes before merge and nothing is deployed automatically.
key_facts.excerpt: Agents trace vulnerabilities through your code and develop patches. Engineers review and test proposed patches before merge... However, patches are not deployed automatically.

key_facts.fact: Greg Brockman said companies 'will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that," OpenAI President Greg Brockman said

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said GPT-6 Cyber scores 52% on the ExploitGym benchmark vs about 38% for Anthropic's Mythos 5.2, and that an upcoming cyber model nearly doubles Mythos 5.2's score.
key_facts.excerpt: able to achieve a much higher performance on this benchmark at 52%. For comparison, Anthropics Mythos 52... scores at about 38%... It demonstrates a significant increase, nearly double the score of Mythos 52.

key_facts.fact: Same day, nonprofits including Public Citizen sued in San Francisco Superior Court to stop OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX's AI businesses from building models more capable than their current best.
key_facts.excerpt: a coalition of nonprofits filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court asking a judge to stop OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceX's AI businesses from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most advanced existing models.

sources.title: OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they're doomed if they don't use them
OpenAI Unveils Daybreak Red Team, Defense Factory Security Tools

stories.headline: Ex-Anthropic researchers' Mirendil raises $1B Series A to automate frontier AI research with agents

key_facts.fact: Mirendil announced a $1B Series A on Nov. 12, led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Google and others participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing that we've raised $1B in a Series A, led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC, and S32

key_facts.fact: The round came about five months after a $200M seed at a $1B valuation; disclosed funding totals about $1.2B.
key_facts.excerpt: The round came about five months after a $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation... Mirendil's disclosed funding to date totals roughly $1.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Founders Behnam Neyshabur and Harsh Mehta left Anthropic in December 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Founders Behnam Neyshabur and Harsh Mehta left Anthropic in December 2025 to start the company in early 2026.

key_facts.fact: Mirendil says one researcher working with agents pretrained Mirendil-Base, a competitive coding model, from scratch in 3.5 months with under $10M in compute.
key_facts.excerpt: One researcher, working with agents, pretrained Mirendil-Base, a competitive coding model, from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10M in compute.

key_facts.fact: Its Lor software, in private beta, runs hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days; its post-trained Fern model holds up to 10M tokens of context.
key_facts.excerpt: post-trained it into Fern, which holds up to 10M tokens of context... And Lor, now in private beta, brings this way of working to everyone else: hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days at a time.

key_facts.fact: The company says agents wrote more than 99% of the code for one project and diagnosed failures with minimal human oversight.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says agents wrote more than 99% of the code for one project, ran the experiments and diagnosed the failures themselves, with minimal human oversight.

sources.title: Mirendil Raises $1B to Democratize Frontier AI R&D
Mirendil Raises $1B Series A for AI Research Agents

stories.headline: Anthropic's automated red-teamer Anvil beats human experts at jailbreaking Claude's safeguards

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 12 Anthropic detailed Anvil, an automated red-teaming system that outperforms human red-teamers against its bioweapons, cybersecurity and distillation safeguards.
key_facts.excerpt: we built Anvil, an automated red-teaming system, which outperforms human red-teamers against our bioweapons, cybersecurity, and distillation safeguards.

key_facts.fact: In biology, Anvil found stronger jailbreaks than all human red-teamers in Anthropic's bug bounty combined, in 24-48 hours instead of weeks to months.
key_facts.excerpt: Anvil finds stronger jailbreaks than all human red-teamers in our bug bounty program combined... finds these jailbreaks in 24–48 hours rather than weeks to months.

key_facts.fact: On cyber tasks, Anvil got the safeguarded model to write working exploits for historical Chrome and Firefox JavaScript-engine bugs, breaking each task in 0.4-4.4 hours where contracted experts took up to 177 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Anvil gets our safeguarded model to write full working exploits of known historical vulnerabilities in the JavaScript engines of Chrome and Firefox... in 0.4–4.4 hours each, where the experts took up to 177 wall-clock hours

key_facts.fact: Against anti-distillation classifiers, Anvil leaked hidden reasoning after 435 requests versus 102,200 for expert red-teamers; training on Anvil cut real-world extraction success on Fable 5.1 from 33.8% to 0%.
key_facts.excerpt: Anvil reached its first substantial reasoning leak after 435 requests (1.2 hours), compared to the 102,200 requests (27.9 hours)... the success rate of reasoning extraction attempts we observed in real traffic fell from 33.8% to 0%.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warns Anvil relies on internal Claude versions with safeguards disabled, and that attackers could soon build similar systems on weaker-safeguarded models.
key_facts.excerpt: It relies on frontier internal versions of Claude with safeguards disabled... suggesting that attackers could soon build similar systems on models with weaker safeguards.

stories.headline: OpenAI raises $15B at $1.25T valuation, half its original $30B target, CNBC reports

key_facts.fact: CNBC's David Faber reported on Nov. 12 that OpenAI has raised $15B at a $1.25 trillion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: CNBC's David Faber delivers his latest 'Faber Report' on OpenAI raising $15B at a valuation of $1.25T

key_facts.fact: OpenAI originally sought up to $30B at a $1.4T valuation, so the raise is half the initial target.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI first went to investors seeking as much as $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, so the final raise is half the original target and below the price it had pitched.

key_facts.fact: The valuation is about 47% above the $852B of OpenAI's March round, when it raised $122B.
key_facts.excerpt: the $1.25 trillion valuation is about 47% above OpenAI's March round, when it raised $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: Sources described it as an opportunistic raise to bridge to an IPO expected in 2027; the round is expected to close within weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: described it as an opportunistic raise to bridge the company to an initial public offering expected in 2027. The round has not formally closed and is expected to wrap up within the next couple of weeks.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has taken about $30B from Nvidia and $65B from SoftBank, according to Faber.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia provided OpenAI with approximately $30 billion, while SoftBank has provided $65 billion, CNBC's David Faber reported.

key_facts.fact: Q3 revenue was about $10B, nearly 50% above Q2, with operating losses of about $10.9B in the quarter per the WSJ.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI took in about $10 billion in the third quarter, nearly 50% more than the previous quarter... operating losses of about $10.9 billion in the quarter, as reported by the Wall Street Journal.

sources.title: Faber Report: OpenAI raised $15B at $1.25T valuation
OpenAI raises $15B at a $1.25T valuation, half its original target, as it bridges to a 2027 IPO
OpenAI Reportedly Raises $15B At $1.25 Trillion Valuation

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO is about six times oversubscribed; bankers to prioritize existing backers

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Nov. 12 that Anthropic's IPO has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available for what could be the largest first-time share sale, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Bankers told prospective investors Anthropic will prioritize existing backers, leaving some buyers with smaller allocations.
key_facts.excerpt: Bankers told prospective investors that Anthropic will prioritize its existing backers, leaving some would-be buyers with smaller allocations than expected

key_facts.fact: Anthropic and some shareholders aim to raise up to $64.4B selling 825M shares at $70-$78, with trading on Nasdaq expected Nov. 19 under ticker ANT.
key_facts.excerpt: aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO by selling 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each. Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on November 19 under the symbol "ANT."

key_facts.fact: A separate $26B private placement, including about $10B from Nvidia, could bring the total to about $90.4B at a fully diluted valuation near $1.4T.
key_facts.excerpt: a separate private placement is expected to bring in another $26 billion. Together, the two transactions could raise around $90.4 billion... Nvidia... has agreed to purchase about $10 billion worth of shares

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's filing reports a revenue run rate of $81B as of Oct. 31, up $10B from end of September.
key_facts.excerpt: The company reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, according to its filing.

key_facts.fact: CEO Dario Amodei is set to join JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in a livestreamed investor event on Friday, Nov. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Dario Amodei, is scheduled to take part in a live-streamed event with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday.

stories.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent can now phone US businesses for paying subscribers

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 12, Meta made outbound calling to US businesses available to all paid Muse subscribers, after testing it with early adopters since September.
key_facts.excerpt: After initially testing the feature in September, Meta's consumer AI agent Muse is now able to place calls to U.S. businesses on behalf of its users. However, only paid subscribers have access to the feature

key_facts.fact: Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang pitched it for calls to cable companies, the DMV, insurers or restaurants without online reservations.
key_facts.excerpt: the feature could be used to take care of calls people don't want to make, like those to their cable company, the DMV, or to a restaurant that doesn't offer online reservations.

key_facts.fact: Muse has over 10 million users; plans start at $20/month for 500M tokens per week, with a $100/month tier for 3B tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's Muse, which now has over 10 million users... Muse subscription plans start at $20 per month for 500 million Muse tokens per week. Heavier AI users can opt to pay $100 per month for 3 billion tokens.

key_facts.fact: Google's Gemini and startup Instinct already offer similar calling; many businesses hang up once they realize an AI is calling.
key_facts.excerpt: the startup Instinct has been offering a similar option, as has Google's Gemini... Many businesses and receptionists hang up on calls from AI agents as soon as they identify that it's not a human on the phone.

sources.title: Muse can now place calls to US businesses — if you pay
